transcript.text: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?

The OE code means the machine cannot drain the water within about 13 minutes, which is why the clothes are sitting in it and the cycle has stopped. The most common cause for this is a blockage in the pump filter (usually at the bottom right) or a kinked drain hose. Since you are worried about flooding, we can try to clear the filter safely without making a mess: switch off and unplug the machine, place a shallow tray or thick towels on the floor in front of the bottom-right filter door, open the flap slowly (expect some water to drip out), and unscrew the filter just a little to let it drain into your tray before removing it fully. Did you find any blockage like coins, lint, or hair in the filter?
I'm not unscrewing the filter, that's what flooded my kitchen last time and I've got laminate. Is there anything else I can try first?

I understand your concern about flooding; we will avoid opening the filter for now. Since OE means the water cannot get out, the next most likely cause is a problem with the drain hose itself rather than the pump. Please check the grey hose at the back of the machine: ensure it isn't kinked or crushed behind the unit, and make sure it isn't pushed too far into your waste pipe (more than 15cm), which can block the flow.
Ok, the machine was pushed right back against the wall and the hose was squashed behind it. I've pulled it out and straightened it. What now?

That’s good progress; straightening the hose removes one obvious restriction. To distinguish between these without opening the filter again: please run a Drain or Spin-only programme. While it is running, listen closely near the bottom of the machine. Can you hear the drain pump humming or buzzing? If you hear it but no water comes out, the pump is likely blocked by something like a coin or hair grip inside. If it is completely silent, the pump motor may have failed.
I tried spin again after straightening it. It drained a little slower than normal and then showed OE again. The pump does hum, and I've heard an occasional rattle too.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The humming with an occasional rattle suggests the pump is trying to work but something is physically blocking or hitting the impeller inside. Because you cannot safely open the filter to clear it without risking a flood on your laminate floor, and because the hose has already been straightened, this is likely a solid object (like a coin or button) lodged deep in the pump housing that you can't reach from the outside. And you are rightly concerned about water damage if we attempt another filter clean, I recommend calling an engineer. They have the tools to safely remove the pump, clear the obstruction, and check if the impeller blades are broken without risking a mess in your kitchen.
